modules.title: Migrations and Schema Evolution
modules.goal: Change production schemas safely, reversibly and without long locks.

topics.title: Migration Basics
topics.simple: Migration schema change ko versioned step me badalta hai.
topics.pro: A migration is a versioned, repeatable change applied in order to every environment.

example.sql:
-- 001_add_student_email.sql
ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN email TEXT;

topics.title: Versioned Migrations
topics.simple: Migration files ka ordered history hota hai.
topics.pro: A migration tool records applied versions so each change runs once per environment.

example.sql: SELECT version, applied_at FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version;

topics.title: Up and Down
topics.simple: Forward aur rollback migration likho.
topics.pro: An up migration applies the change and a down migration reverses it when safe.

example.sql:
-- up: ADD COLUMN email TEXT
-- down: DROP COLUMN email

topics.title: Idempotency
topics.simple: Migration dobara chalne par safe hona chahiye.
topics.pro: Idempotent migrations use IF NOT EXISTS and guards so a retry does not fail halfway.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email TEXT;

topics.title: Adding Columns
topics.simple: Naye column ko nullable ya default ke saath add karo.
topics.pro: Adding a nullable column is cheap; adding NOT NULL with a volatile default can rewrite or lock the table.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email TEXT;

topics.title: Dropping Columns
topics.simple: Column drop karne se pehle usage check karo.
topics.pro: Dropping a column breaks dependent code and views, so expand-contract and deprecate first.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS legacy_email;

topics.title: Renaming
topics.simple: Rename ko expand-contract se karo.
topics.pro: Renaming a column or table breaks old code; add the new name, dual-write, migrate readers, then remove the old one.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students RENAME COLUMN email TO contact_email;

topics.title: Backfills
topics.simple: Backfill data ko batches me karo.
topics.pro: A backfill updates existing rows in small batches to avoid long locks and huge transactions.

example.sql: UPDATE students SET email = 'unknown@example.com' WHERE id BETWEEN 1 AND 1000 AND email IS NULL;

topics.title: Online Migrations
topics.simple: Live traffic ke saath migration plan karo.
topics.pro: Online migrations avoid long exclusive locks and keep the old and new shapes compatible during rollout.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_students_email ON students (email);

topics.title: Locks
topics.simple: Migrations locks ko samajh kar chalao.
topics.pro: ALTER TABLE often takes a lock that blocks reads or writes; check lock levels and set lock_timeout.

example.sql: SET lock_timeout = '5s';

topics.title: Transactions
topics.simple: Transactional DDL use karo jahan possible ho.
topics.pro: PostgreSQL supports transactional DDL, so a failed migration can roll back cleanly; concurrent index builds are an exception.

topics.title: Rollbacks
topics.simple: Rollback plan deploy se pehle likho.
topics.pro: A rollback plan covers code, schema and data, and is tested before production.

example.sql:
-- down migration
ALTER TABLE students DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS email;

topics.title: Data Migrations
topics.simple: Schema change ke saath data transform karo.
topics.pro: Data migrations move or reshape values, often in batches with validation before and after.

example.sql: UPDATE students SET marks = 0 WHERE marks IS NULL;

topics.title: Zero-Downtime
topics.simple: Expand, migrate, contract sequence follow karo.
topics.pro: Zero-downtime changes add compatible structures, migrate data and readers, then remove the old structures.

example.sql: -- 1 add new column, 2 backfill, 3 switch code, 4 drop old

topics.title: Expand and Contract
topics.simple: Compatibility window rakho.
topics.pro: The expand-contract pattern keeps old and new schemas working together during deployment.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN contact_email TEXT;

topics.title: Testing Migrations
topics.simple: Migrations ko real data copy par test karo.
topics.pro: Test on a production-like snapshot, measure lock time and verify both up and down paths.

example.sql: -- run migration against a staging snapshot

topics.title: Migration Tools
topics.simple: Tool version, lock aur transaction behavior samjho.
topics.pro: Tools such as Flyway, Liquibase, Alembic and Prisma differ in transaction handling, locking and rollback support.

example.sql: SELECT * FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version;

topics.title: Production Checklist
topics.simple: Backup, lock timeout, monitoring aur rollback ready rakho.
topics.pro: A production migration checklist covers backup, compatibility, lock timeouts, observability and a tested rollback.

example.sql:
SET statement_timeout = '30s';
SET lock_timeout = '5s';

topics.title: Common Migration Errors
topics.simple: Long locks, missing defaults aur irreversible drops common errors hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are rewriting a large table, adding NOT NULL without a backfill, and dropping a column still used by old code.

example.sql: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email TEXT;

topics.title: Practical Migration
topics.simple: Add a column, backfill, constrain and switch code.
topics.pro: A practical migration adds a nullable column, backfills in batches, adds the constraint, deploys code and removes the old path.

example.sql:
ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS contact_email TEXT;
UPDATE students SET contact_email = email WHERE contact_email IS NULL;

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Migration Basics in a production query.
interview.answer: A migration is a versioned, repeatable change applied in order to every environment. Key rules: One change per migration. Version the file. Apply in order.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Versioned Migrations in a production query.
interview.answer: A migration tool records applied versions so each change runs once per environment. Key rules: Use numeric prefixes. Store applied versions. Never edit applied migrations.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Up and Down in a production query.
interview.answer: An up migration applies the change and a down migration reverses it when safe. Key rules: Write both directions. Test the down path. Some data changes are irreversible.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Idempotency in a production query.
interview.answer: Idempotent migrations use IF NOT EXISTS and guards so a retry does not fail halfway. Key rules: Use IF NOT EXISTS. Guard data changes. Record completion.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Adding Columns in a production query.
interview.answer: Adding a nullable column is cheap; adding NOT NULL with a volatile default can rewrite or lock the table. Key rules: Add nullable first. Backfill separately. Add NOT NULL last.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Dropping Columns in a production query.
interview.answer: Dropping a column breaks dependent code and views, so expand-contract and deprecate first. Key rules: Search usage. Deploy code first. Drop after a grace period.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Renaming in a production query.
interview.answer: Renaming a column or table breaks old code; add the new name, dual-write, migrate readers, then remove the old one. Key rules: Add new. Dual-write. Migrate readers. Remove old.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Backfills in a production query.
interview.answer: A backfill updates existing rows in small batches to avoid long locks and huge transactions. Key rules: Batch by key. Commit each batch. Make it resumable.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Online Migrations in a production query.
interview.answer: Online migrations avoid long exclusive locks and keep the old and new shapes compatible during rollout. Key rules: Use concurrent index builds. Avoid table rewrites. Deploy compatible code.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Locks in a production query.
interview.answer: ALTER TABLE often takes a lock that blocks reads or writes; check lock levels and set lock_timeout. Key rules: Know the lock level. Set lock_timeout. Run at low traffic.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Transactions in a production query.
interview.answer: PostgreSQL supports transactional DDL, so a failed migration can roll back cleanly; concurrent index builds are an exception. Key rules: Wrap in a transaction. Check tool behavior. Avoid long transactions.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Rollbacks in a production query.
interview.answer: A rollback plan covers code, schema and data, and is tested before production. Key rules: Test the down migration. Keep backups. Know the recovery time.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Data Migrations in a production query.
interview.answer: Data migrations move or reshape values, often in batches with validation before and after. Key rules: Validate before. Transform in batches. Verify counts.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Zero-Downtime in a production query.
interview.answer: Zero-downtime changes add compatible structures, migrate data and readers, then remove the old structures. Key rules: Expand. Dual-write. Migrate. Contract.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Expand and Contract in a production query.
interview.answer: The expand-contract pattern keeps old and new schemas working together during deployment. Key rules: Add before removing. Support both readers. Remove after verification.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Testing Migrations in a production query.
interview.answer: Test on a production-like snapshot, measure lock time and verify both up and down paths. Key rules: Use realistic data. Measure duration. Test rollback.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Migration Tools in a production query.
interview.answer: Tools such as Flyway, Liquibase, Alembic and Prisma differ in transaction handling, locking and rollback support. Key rules: Know the tool. Review generated SQL. Keep migrations in version control.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Production Checklist in a production query.
interview.answer: A production migration checklist covers backup, compatibility, lock timeouts, observability and a tested rollback. Key rules: Backup first. Set lock_timeout. Watch errors. Have a rollback.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Common Migration Errors in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are rewriting a large table, adding NOT NULL without a backfill, and dropping a column still used by old code. Key rules: Avoid rewrites. Backfill first. Deprecate before dropping.

interview.q: Module 31 · Explain Practical Migration in a production query.
interview.answer: A practical migration adds a nullable column, backfills in batches, adds the constraint, deploys code and removes the old path. Key rules: Add nullable. Backfill. Constrain. Deploy. Clean up.

debug.title: Long lock
debug.broken: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN email TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT md5(random()::text);
debug.error: A volatile default can rewrite the table under a lock

debug.title: Non-concurrent index
debug.fix: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_students_email ON students (email);

debug.title: Drop before code
debug.broken: ALTER TABLE students DROP COLUMN email;
debug.fix: Deploy code that no longer reads email, wait, then drop the column.
debug.error: Old application instances still query email

debug.title: Missing IF NOT EXISTS
debug.broken: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN email TEXT;
debug.fix: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email TEXT;

debug.title: Backfill in one transaction
debug.broken: UPDATE students SET email = 'unknown@example.com' WHERE email IS NULL;
debug.fix: Batch by id and commit each batch.
debug.error: A huge transaction holds locks and bloats WAL

debug.title: Rename breaks readers
debug.broken: ALTER TABLE students RENAME COLUMN email TO contact_email;
debug.fix: Add contact_email, dual-write, migrate readers, then remove email.

debug.title: Lock timeout missing
debug.broken: ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN email TEXT;
debug.fix:
SET lock_timeout = '5s';
ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN email TEXT;
debug.error: The migration can wait behind a long transaction

debug.title: Concurrent in transaction
debug.fix: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_students_email ON students (email);
debug.error: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block

debug.title: No verification
debug.broken: Run the migration and deploy immediately.
debug.fix: Verify row counts, constraints and application errors before removing the old path.
debug.error: The change may be silently incomplete
